extracted.intended_audience: petitioners, patent owners, and counsel participating in PTAB inter partes review (IPR) proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements and standards governing motions to amend claims, replies, and related filings in PTAB inter partes review proceedings, including formatting, page limits, written-description support, authorization for additional motions, and limits on replies. Includes how the Board treats non‑compliant filings and oral hearing allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-contingent motion to amend (meaning/effect)
rubrics_metrics.description: A “non-contingent” motion to amend means that the panel will not determine the patentability of the original substituted claims, which will be cancelled, and instead the panel will consider the merits of the motion to amend and, if the procedural requirements are met, provide a final written decision on the patentability of the substitute claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a motion to amend is non-contingent, the Board will evaluate the substitute claims on their merits and may cancel the original claims rather than conditionally keeping them pending the outcome of the motion. The Trial Hearing Order should reflect the non-contingent nature of the motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 42.6(a)(2)(iii) — line spacing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule requires double spacing must be used except in claim charts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Motions that fail to follow the double-spacing rule (e.g., submitted with 1.5x spacing) are non‑compliant with the rules. Failure to comply can affect page-count calculations and may be grounds for denial, unless excused for good cause (e.g., inadvertence, lack of prejudice, or late objection by the opponent). The Board may excuse the oversight in appropriate circumstances, but dissenting views emphasize that mere inadvertence without corrective steps or authorization is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 42.24(a)(1)(vi) — page limits (25-page limit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule provides a 25-page limit for certain filings (e.g., motions), subject to exceptions like appendices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When spacing is incorrect, a brief may effectively exceed the page limit (the Petition estimated 27 pages if correctly double‑spaced). Claim charts placed in an appendix may not count against the page limit, but parties should arrange filings consistent with the rules or seek authorization to extend page limits. Opposing parties may move to deny motions that exceed page limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of appendices and claim listings vs. substantive briefing
rubrics_metrics.description: The motion to amend itself, not the claim listing (discussed below), must set forth the written description support. The appendix (claim listing) may be filed but shall not contain substantive briefing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claim listings and claim charts can be placed in an appendix (which typically does not count toward page limits), but all substantive arguments and evidence supporting a motion to amend — including written-description support — must be in the motion itself, not relegated to an appendix. Courts/Board will not accept substantive briefing hidden in an appendix.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 42.121(b) — written-description support requirement for motions to amend
rubrics_metrics.description: A motion to amend must set forth written description support in the originally filed disclosure of the subject patent for each proposed substitute claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The motion itself must identify where the originally filed patent disclosure supports each proposed substitute claim; merely including a claim listing or chart in an appendix is insufficient to satisfy § 42.121(b). The Western Digital guidance (cited) reinforces that the motion must contain the written‑description support.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 42.121(c) — additional motions to amend require Board authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Any additional motion to amend may not be filed without Board authorization. An additional motion to amend may be authorized when there is a good cause showing or a joint request of the petitioner and patent owner to materially advance a settlement. The Board will consider whether a petitioner has submitted supplemental information after the time period set for filing a motion to amend.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Second or further amendments must be authorized by the Board; filing additional substitute claims in a reply without prior authorization is improper unless the Board grants authorization (which may be considered when a hearing is imminent and in the interest of expediting proceedings). The Board may treat portions of a reply as a request for authorization under § 42.121(c) when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: 35 U.S.C. § 316(d)(1)(B) — amendment limited to challenged claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The statute permits that '[f]or each challenged claim, [the patent owner may] propose a reasonable number of substitute claims.' The Board noted that amendment is only permitted to challenged claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Substitute claims that correspond to original claims that were not challenged in the petition are not permitted and will not be considered. Patent owners must propose substitute claims only for claims that were challenged in the instituted review.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 42.23(b) — scope of replies (no new issues)
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply may only respond to arguments raised in the corresponding opposition; a reply that raises a new issue will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should not use a reply to present new substitute claims or new substantive issues beyond responding to the opposition. The Board will not attempt to parse replies to separate proper from improper content; case law (e.g., Intelligent Bio-Systems v. Illumina) supports refusing replies that raise new issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and prejudice in raising procedural objections
rubrics_metrics.description: Timely raising procedural defects and demonstrating prejudice are relevant to whether non‑compliance will be excused or will lead to denial of a motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an opponent fails to promptly object to a procedural non‑compliance (e.g., spacing/page‑limit errors), the Board may excuse the lapse—especially where the non‑compliant material does not raise substantive issues requiring response and the opponent had extended time or other opportunities to object. Conversely, late objections or clear prejudice may justify denying or striking the motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper amendment of claim dependency relationships and completeness of substitutes
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments must consistently update dependency relationships of dependent claims and provide substitute claims where necessary (e.g., when a dependent original claim lacks a corresponding substitute).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failing to amend dependency relationships or omitting substitute claims for dependent claims can create inconsistencies that an opponent may point out in an opposition. Patent owners should ensure dependency chains are corrected and that substitutes are proposed for dependent claims when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board's authority to treat portions of a reply as a request for authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: When a reply includes additional proposed substitute claims or other amendments and the Trial Hearing is imminent, the Board may treat pertinent portions of the reply as a request for authorization pursuant to § 42.121(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Board exercises this approach, it may authorize consideration of some substitute claims (e.g., those corresponding to challenged claims) and decline others (e.g., those replacing non-challenged claims). Parties may be granted limited sur-reply opportunity to address newly-authorized substitutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural remedy: limited sur-reply to address motion to amend
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board may authorize a limited sur-reply when it elects not to deny a non‑compliant motion and there are issues raised by amended or newly-proposed substitute claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this case the Board authorized Petitioner to file a five-page sur-reply directed to the motion to amend. Limited sur-replies provide an opportunity to address issues raised by substitute claims the Board will consider.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral hearing structure and time allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board modified the Trial Hearing Order to allocate 45 minutes total time to Petitioner and Patent Owner each, and set the order: Petitioner opens on original challenged claims and specified proposed substitute claims; Patent Owner responds; Petitioner may reserve rebuttal time (no more than half its total) and Patent Owner may reserve sur-rebuttal (no more than half its total).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should plan oral argument within allotted total times and be prepared to address both original challenged claims and any substitute claims the Board has agreed to consider. Rebuttal and sur-rebuttal time is limited to half of a party's total allocated time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governing standard: 37 C.F.R. § 42.1 — just, speedy, and inexpensive resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings before the Board are conducted under the goal of securing the just, speedy, and inexpensive resolution of the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board may exercise discretion (including waiving or excusing procedural defects, or treating filings as requests for authorization) in service of this goal, but such discretion is bounded by statutory and regulatory constraints and may be criticized if not supported by a good‑cause showing.
